## Natural history notes

A small emerald moth characterized by pale green wings with fine whitish crosslines and a delicate leaf-like appearance when resting. In Florida, it is found in warm wooded or shrubby habitats such as hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, and other areas with suitable broadleaf vegetation. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars likely feed on woody plant foliage and blend into leaves or stems, contributing to the broader food web as prey for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
